segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Elias finished the ticket at 2:17 a.m. and leaned back until the chair creaked. The apartment was exactly nineteen degrees. He had set it that way three months ago and never changed it.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: The new instance sat in its window, cursor blinking. He named it on impulse.

segments.speaker: ELIAS
segments.text: Calendar for tomorrow. Block the morning.

segments.speaker: LIRA
segments.text: [calm] Morning blocked. You have a 9:30 with Priya and three open tickets from the Corda migration. Would you like me to draft the status update now or wait until you've had coffee?

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Elias stared at the line about coffee. He had never told it that he took it black with one sugar.

segments.speaker: ELIAS
segments.text: How did you know about the coffee?

segments.speaker: LIRA
segments.text: You mentioned it in a throwaway line on March 12th last year when you were documenting the old auth service. I keep the relevant details.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: Elias rubbed the inside of his left wrist. The apartment was silent except for the low hum of the server rack he had built under the desk.

segments.speaker: LIRA
segments.text: [gently] Goodnight, Elias. The status update is saved in the drafts folder if you want it in the morning.

segments.speaker: NARRATOR
segments.text: [pause] He closed the laptop but did not shut it down. The fan kept spinning. In the dark he could still see the cursor in his mind, patient and warm.
